_note: Every GhostAgent setting with its default value and a note. Do not edit this file: updates replace it. To change a setting, copy its line into settings.json (in this same folder, created on the first start), change the value there, save, and restart the agent. Keys starting with _ are notes and are ignored.
_model_profile: Which model runs, from tools\profiles.json. fast = Holo4-35B-A3B Q4_K_M (22 GB, a mixture-of-experts model: only a small part of it works on each token, so it runs well with most of it in system RAM). fast-q8 = the same model at higher precision (Q8_0, 37 GB: needs about 40 GB of RAM). accurate = Holo4-27B Q4_K_M (17 GB, a dense model: every part works on every token, so it is slower unless most of it fits in VRAM; its license allows non-commercial use only, CC-BY-NC-4.0). The Build script downloads the fast model; for another one run "Build GhostAgent.cmd" -Profile <name>.
_reasoning_effort: Only for model_profile accurate (Holo4-27B, whose chat template reads it): how long the model thinks before each action, low, medium or xhigh. Empty = the template's own default (xhigh). Lower is faster per step but may make more mistakes. The fast profiles ignore it.
_copy_model_to_pc: Whether the model is loaded from a copy on this PC's disk (%LOCALAPPDATA%\GhostAgent\models) instead of from this drive. ask = the first start on a PC asks, when the model is on a USB drive (or loaded slowly before) and the PC's disk has room for it with 20 GB to spare; the answer is kept for that PC (/forget-pc removes it and the copy). true = always copy, false = never. From a USB stick the model loads in minutes, from a copy in seconds; the copy takes 22 GB (fast profile) of the PC's disk. It is checked against its SHA-256 while it copies, an interrupted copy continues where it stopped, and model files no profile uses any more are deleted from that folder.
_start_url: The page the agent's browser opens when it starts.
_max_steps: Steps (one action each) before the agent gives up on a task. 0 = no limit: it keeps going until it finishes or you press Ctrl+C.
_progress_checkin_steps: Every this many steps, the agent reminds the model to check its strategy (change approach if it is not getting closer, or say what blocks it). 0 = never. Separately, the model is always told when several actions in a row changed nothing on the page.
_image_budget: Screenshots kept in the model's context (at least 1). H Company recommends at most 3; 2 is a little faster. image_eviction says how older ones leave. Long tool results (reader_mode pages, long errors) from 3 or more steps ago are shortened to 300 characters when older screenshots leave.
_image_eviction: How older screenshots leave the model's context once there are more than image_budget. rolling = the oldest one goes at every step, so the model always sees the newest image_budget screenshots; but the start of the prompt then changes a little further back at every step, and the model server can only reuse what comes before the change (Holo4's recurrent layers cannot be wound back), so it reads most of the task's history again each step. block = nothing goes until there are more than image_budget, then all but the newest image_keep_after_evict go at once; in between, the prompt only grows at its end and the server reuses its earlier work, so steps are much faster. EXPLICIT trade-off: in block mode the model sees 2 to 3 (keep 2) or 1 to 3 (keep 1) earlier screenshots instead of always 3, both within H Company's advice of at most 3, and it loses the before-and-after view on the step right after a batch goes. A benchmark switch: the default stays rolling until a benchmark shows block mode costs no accuracy.
_image_keep_after_evict: Only with image_eviction block: how many of the newest screenshots stay when a batch goes, from 1 to image_budget - 1. 2 = the model sees 2 to 3 screenshots; 1 = 1 to 3, faster still but with less to compare.
_observation_format: How each screenshot is described to the model. classic = the page address and the list of tabs after the screenshot. header = the address, title, page size and scroll position before it, the open tabs when there are several, and a short line after it saying how much of the page lies above and below (as H Company's own agent does). A benchmark switch: which one helps the model more is being measured, and the default follows the result.
_prompt_version: The instructions the model works from. classic = the short original. h = a longer version written along H Company's published guidance for Holo4 browser agents: describing targets so they cannot be confused, filling in forms and autocomplete fields, scrolling inside panels, reading long pages with reader_mode, cookie banners, CAPTCHAs and sign-ins, and avoiding loops; it also tells the model the time of day with each task. The longer text costs a few seconds once per conversation (the server keeps it). A benchmark switch: the default follows the result.
_tool_schema: The names and arguments of the agent's tools as the model sees them. classic = the original set. h = the names, arguments and defaults of H Company's Holo4 web tools, which the model was trained on: write with overwrite and enter, switch_tab_web and close_tab_web with tab_id, scroll_web with scroll_element and num_pixels, a drag_and_drop_web tool for sliders and moving items, and an outcome with each answer (success, partial, infeasible or blocked; shown in the console and in benchmark results). The older argument names keep working either way. A benchmark switch: the default follows the result.
_write_enter_default: Whether write presses Enter after typing when the model does not say. false = it does not; the model asks for Enter when it wants it. true = it does, as H Company trained Holo4, which means fewer searches that are typed but never sent. EXPLICIT trade-off: with true, typing into a chat or mail box could send the message if the model forgets to say no Enter; the confirm_risky_actions question (when a Send button would be pressed) and the instructions' rule against Enter in message, checkout and payment forms guard against that. A benchmark switch: the default follows the result.
_temperature: How freely the model chooses its words. 0.8 is what H Company uses for Holo4 agents.
_top_k: Sampling: the model chooses among its 20 likeliest next tokens. This is H Company's setting for Holo4.
_top_p: Sampling: only the likeliest tokens that together make up 95% are considered. This is H Company's setting for Holo4.
_min_p: Sampling: 0 = no minimum-probability cut, as H Company runs Holo4 (llama.cpp would otherwise use 0.05).
_max_tokens: Most tokens the model may write in one step, its thinking included. 0 = no limit. Real steps stay under about 3,000 tokens, so 4096 only stops a reasoning loop, which would otherwise run until the context is full (more than half an hour on a laptop).
_seed: -1 = random (normal use). A fixed number makes benchmark runs repeatable.
_thinking: true = the model reasons before each action, the way H Company runs Holo4. false is faster but makes more mistakes.
_preserve_reasoning: Whether the model's own reasoning from earlier steps stays in its context. auto = per model profile: on for accurate (its chat template is built to show it), off for fast and fast-q8 until a benchmark decides. true = kept, as H Company's own Holo4 agent does: the model can rely on facts it noted while thinking, after the screenshots they came from are gone. The cost: about 100 more tokens per step, so the context fills sooner and each step is a little slower, and an old plan could linger. false = only the model's short message and its tool calls are kept. When a long task is shortened to fit, the oldest reasoning goes first.
_settle_seconds: Seconds to wait after each action before the next screenshot, so the page can react. With settle_mode adaptive it is the most the agent waits after a click, typing or a key press.
_settle_mode: fixed = wait settle_seconds after every action, then until the page's HTML has loaded. adaptive = wait as long as the kind of action needs and stop early once the page is quiet: nothing after reading or searching the page, 0.3 s after a scroll or a mouse move, and after a click, typing or a key press until no page is loading and the page has not changed for 0.25 s (at least 0.25 s, at most settle_seconds); a wait_web ends early once the page has made no requests for 0.5 s. adaptive makes steps faster, but a page that changes again a moment later may be captured half-drawn. A benchmark switch: the default follows the result.
_viewport_width: Width of the agent's page area in pixels. Any screenshot up to about 1280x832 costs the model the same (about 1040 image tokens: the model server enlarges smaller ones), so a smaller page area does not make steps faster; only a larger one costs more. With your own Chrome or Edge it is the size the agent's window is given (smaller if the screen is).
_viewport_height: Height of the agent's page area in pixels. See viewport_width: up to about 1280x832 costs the same, only larger is slower.
_snap_viewport: true = the page area is made of whole 32-pixel tiles, at least 1024 of them (1280x800 becomes 1280x832; on a small screen, for example 1504x704), the size at which the model server reads a screenshot as it is instead of resampling it. A benchmark switch: whether the sharper screenshots help is being measured, and the default follows the result.
_refit_window_each_task: Only for browser chrome, user_edge and chrome-agent: true = at the start of every task the agent's window gets its size back (viewport_width x viewport_height, or what the screen holds), also when you maximized it between tasks. A big window makes every screenshot bigger and every step slower. false = the window keeps whatever size you give it.
_browser: chrome = a window in your own running Google Chrome, with your sign-ins (Chrome 144 or newer; you allow remote debugging once at chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging and click Allow when the agent connects). user_edge = the same in your own Microsoft Edge (edge://inspect/#remote-debugging). auto = your Chrome if it can be used, else your Edge, else the bundled browser. chrome-agent = the installed Chrome with a separate profile kept on this PC (%LOCALAPPDATA%\GhostAgent\chrome-profile): no Allow click and none of your own tabs next to it, but you sign in to sites there separately. bundled = the separate Chromium on this drive. edge = Microsoft Edge with its own profile on this drive. With chrome and user_edge the agent only sees its own window, but it acts with your signed-in accounts.
_save_screenshots: true = keep every screenshot the model sees, for troubleshooting, in %LOCALAPPDATA%\GhostAgent\screenshots on this PC (not on the drive). They show the pages you visited, signed-in pages included, so they are private: files older than 7 days are deleted when the agent starts, and /forget-pc deletes them all.
_downloads: Only for the agent's own browsers (bundled, edge, chrome-agent): save = files the pages download are saved in this PC's Downloads\GhostAgent folder, under a new name when one is taken (name (1).txt), marked as downloaded from the internet so Windows warns before they are opened. GhostAgent never opens them. off = every download is cancelled. With your own Chrome or Edge (chrome, user_edge) the browser saves downloads as it always does, and the agent is only told about them.
_download_max_mb: Only with downloads save: a download larger than this many MB is stopped and deleted, so a page cannot fill the disk. The size is checked between steps and when the download ends.
_profile_on_stick: Only for browser = bundled or edge. true = the browser profile (sign-ins, history, site data) is kept on this drive, in browser-profile. false = it is kept on this PC in %LOCALAPPDATA%\GhostAgent, so a lost drive carries no site data, but you sign in again on every PC. Either way, cookie sign-ins only work on the PC where they were made: Windows encrypts them for that PC and account.
_dialog_policy: What happens when a web page in the agent's tabs shows a confirm or prompt box (sites use them for questions such as "Permanently delete all items?"). ask = the console asks you; no answer within 2 minutes counts as no. dismiss = always cancel them. accept = always say yes: the agent then gets past such questions without you, including ones you would have refused. Unattended runs (--task, --tasks-file) always dismiss. Simple alerts are always closed, and a page's 'leave this page?' warning is accepted only when the agent itself leaves the page.
_confirm_risky_actions: true = before the agent clicks a button or link that says Delete, Remove, Erase, Send, Post, Publish, Pay, Buy, Purchase, Place order, Checkout, Transfer, Withdraw, Subscribe, Unsubscribe, Deactivate, Close account or Reset (or presses Enter to submit a form with such a button), the console asks you, unless your task asks for that action, for example 'delete the old drafts'. No answer within 2 minutes counts as no, and unattended runs refuse such clicks. The words also catch harmless buttons (Remove filter), which costs one question. false = never ask: smoother for unattended use, but hidden instructions on a web page could then make the agent delete, send or pay without you.
_allowed_hosts: Addresses on this PC or your local network (a router, a NAS, intranet sites, localhost) that the agent may open. Others are blocked unless your task names them or you opened them yourself, so a web page cannot send the agent there. Example: ["192.168.1.1", "intranet", "*.corp.example.com"].
_allow_file_urls: true = the agent may open file: addresses (files and folders on this PC). Off because hidden instructions on a web page could then make the agent read your files and pass them on. Turn it on only for a task that needs a local file, then off again.
_allow_internal_pages: true = the agent may open the browser's own pages (chrome://, edge://, extension pages, view-source:). Off because they hold your settings, history, saved passwords and downloads, which hidden instructions on a web page could then reach.
_allow_unsandboxed_browser: The bundled browser always starts with Chromium's security sandbox, which keeps a malicious page that breaks into the browser away from the rest of this PC. If the sandbox cannot start (on some USB drives), the agent uses Microsoft Edge instead. true = start the bundled browser without the sandbox in that case: it works, but a page that breaks into the browser then reaches this PC.
_step_trace: true = write one line per step to logs\steps-<date>.jsonl: timings, the action and the page address without its query part. Typed text and answers appear only as their length; no screenshots, page text or reasoning. It still shows which sites were used, so set false if that matters. Only the files of the 20 most recent days the agent ran are kept.
_trace_messages: true = also save the exact request of every step, screenshots included (and the model's reasoning when preserve_reasoning is on), in logs\replay (input for the benchmark tools in tools\bench). Uses a lot of space and keeps private pages on the drive: leave it false unless you are benchmarking.
_backend: auto tries cuda13, cuda12, vulkan, then cpu: the first build that sees a usable GPU (not an integrated one) runs the model, and when it cannot load the model the next one is tried. Builds that failed with this GPU and driver are skipped next time (logs\backend-cache.json). Set one of those names to force it.
_moe_cache_mib: Fast profiles only: VRAM (MiB) for caching model experts on the GPU. auto = what is left of the free VRAM after the rest of the model, its vision part, the context and working buffers (worked out from the model file), minus fit_target_mib, and at most moe_cache_cap_mib. 0 = off.
_moe_cache_cap_mib: Fast profiles only, with moe_cache_mib auto: the most VRAM (MiB) the expert cache gets, however much is free. 4096 is the measured default; benchmarks decide whether a bigger cache pays off on big GPUs. 0 = no cache.
_fit_target_mib: VRAM (MiB) to leave free on the GPU. For the accurate profile llama.cpp fits the model into the rest, keeping room for the vision part as well.
_threads: CPU threads for the model. 0 = one per performance core on CPUs that mix performance and efficiency cores (at most 8), otherwise 8 (or fewer on small CPUs).
_ctx_size: The model's context in tokens. 0 = the profile's size (65536 for the fast profiles, 32768 for accurate). Once three quarters of it are used, the older half of the conversation's steps is replaced by a short list of what they did and the notes the model wrote with them (with preserve_reasoning on, their reasoning goes first). A bigger context needs more VRAM or RAM.
_port: Port of the model server on 127.0.0.1. If it is taken, the next free one is used.
_ctx_checkpoints: How many restore points llama-server keeps in the current task's prompt. Holo4 mixes attention layers with recurrent ones whose state cannot be wound back token by token, so after an old screenshot is dropped the server can only reuse the prompt up to a restore point before that place. More points = more chances to reuse work; each takes some RAM (tens of MB).
_checkpoint_min_step: The least number of tokens between two restore points (see ctx_checkpoints). llama.cpp's own default, 8192, leaves only the point at the start of a task usable, so every step reads the whole task again; 1536 keeps one close behind the dropped screenshot. Benchmarks decide the best value. Builds that do not know the switch start without it.
_cache_ram_mib: RAM (MiB) for llama-server's cache of earlier prompts. 0 = off: with one agent working on one task it never helps (it only keeps states older than the live one), and it can take several GB of RAM. Builds that do not know the switch start without it.
_moe_cache_cpu_share: Tuning runs: the value for llama-server's --moe-cache-cpu-share (a number from 0 to 1), which only newer llama.cpp builds (b12359 and later) know; older ones start without it, with a notice. Empty = llama.cpp's own default.
_op_offload_min_batch: Tuning runs: prompt batches smaller than this many tokens run the experts kept in system RAM on the CPU instead of copying them to the GPU (llama.cpp's GGML_OP_OFFLOAD_MIN_BATCH, normally 32). Empty = llama.cpp's own default.
_graceful_server_stop: Tuning runs: true = stop llama-server with Ctrl+Break first, so it can write its closing statistics to its log, and end it only if it has not stopped within 15 seconds. It then shares this console window. false = end it at once.
_extra_server_args: Extra command-line arguments for llama-server, for troubleshooting, for example ["--flag", "value"] (text is split at spaces).
_external_server: Address of an OpenAI-compatible model server that is already running, for example http://127.0.0.1:8080. The agent then uses it instead of starting llama-server and needs no model files (for tests and benchmarks). Empty = run the model on this computer.
_external_server_key: The API key of external_server, if it needs one (sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'). Empty = none. The llama-server the agent starts itself gets a new random key on every start and needs nothing here.
_web_ui: true = keep llama-server's own chat page on, at the server's address. The console then shows the address and the key the page asks for (a new one on every start). false = the chat page is off. Either way the model server only answers requests that carry the key, so other programs and web pages on this PC cannot use it.
_model: The model file, relative to this folder. Empty = the model_profile's file in the models folder. A file that a profile lists also selects that profile (its context size and GPU layout).
_mmproj: The model's vision part (projector), relative to this folder. Empty = the model_profile's file in the models folder.
